passage:
Email 1 — From Mariam, Student Technology Club, to Engineer Hassan.

Dear Engineer Hassan,
Our class is planning a small exhibition about changes in city transport. We have built a model bus shelter with a digital information board and a solar lamp. The idea is to make travelling easier for visitors, but some residents are worried about the cost. We collected opinions from thirty volunteers at the community centre, and their main concern was what would happen if the screen stopped working.

Our first plan showed departure times only on the screen. We now think printed timetables should also be available. Would you review our design and explain which features are likely to work in different weather conditions?

Best wishes,
Mariam

Email 2 — From Engineer Hassan to Mariam.

Dear Mariam,
A backup timetable is a sensible decision. Digital services can improve access, but they must not prevent people without smartphones from using public transport. Your model should include information in clear language, with large lettering and simple directions. If the display uses solar electricity, remember that the output changes when clouds reduce sunlight. You should measure performance at different times instead of claiming that one panel will always be sufficient.

I also suggest inviting people with different accessibility needs to test the shelter. A technology project is only successful when its users can understand and operate it.

Kind regards,
Hassan

Email 3 — From Mariam to Engineer Hassan.

Dear Engineer Hassan,
Thank you for your comments. We tested the solar lamp during three afternoons and found that it became noticeably dimmer under heavy cloud. We added a small battery so the display could remain visible when the model received less light. Our teacher helped us label the chart as classroom data, not a prediction about a real bus network.

We also asked five older visitors to review the directions. Two preferred printed information, while others liked the idea of audio announcements. After their feedback, we changed the colour contrast and added a large printed route map. We will show the revised model to families next Monday. What should we explain about the information the display collects?

Best wishes,
Mariam

Email 4 — From Engineer Hassan to Mariam.

Dear Mariam,
It is important to separate useful measurements from personal data. A model can record sunlight and battery levels without storing a passenger's name, telephone number or travel history. If a future service collects such information, its operators will need clear rules about consent and secure storage. For your exhibition, display exactly what the sensors measure and what they do not measure.

Invite visitors to compare the original model with the revised version. Explain which changes resulted from evidence and which remain suggestions for future testing. Your project will then show how technology, energy choices and public feedback can work together without promising an unrealistic solution for every city.

With best wishes,
Hassan
